THE STATE AT LARGE

Returns BY counties, completed or partial.
Official or estimated, came more fully yesterday and brought something like order out of the chaos that ruled the Minnesota election returns Tuesday night. Below is given a table OF majorities BY counties, which are approximately and proportionately accurate, and consolidated into majorities which are more likely to be increased than diminished. The most extraordinary thing in the whole showing is the reduction of White's majority in the first district. He is elected, but only by the skin of his teeth. Bierman has made a still hunt of singular success, and with few weeks more to work would probably have secured his election. The natural theory of this result is that Dunnell has been engaged in undermining White, but he denies this, and the returns from the different counties give some color of truth to his denial. Bierman's gains have been in the Democratic and Scandinavian nationalists, and to belief among the Democrats that the disaffection of the Dunnell and anti-Windom men generally gave them a chance. Winona, ordinarily a close county, gives Bierman over 1000 majority and Republican publican majorities in Dodge, Freeborn, Houston, Mower and Olmsted are reduced to a few hundred each, and White is only saved from defeat by 800 majority in Fillmore county. It appears that Bierman's agents did not get around to the Fillmore county Scandinavians.

In the second and third districts the returns run about as usual, except in Blue Earth and a few other counties, where the result is complicated by local issues. Returns from some three or four counties in each district, and partial returns from these, give Wakefield and Strait about 4,500 and 500 respectively. Probably the complete returns will add 1000 to each of these.

In the fourth district, Washburn's majority slightly exceeds the conservative estimate made last night. Hennepin gives him 5,900, which is more than offset by 1,900 for Ames in Ramsey. Estimates for the other counties, however, place his majority at 2,624. Wright gives him over 900 majority by the official count and Sibley 50. Reasonable estimates for Chisago, Anoka, Isanti and the others make up the rest.

The fifth district exceeds all reasonable expectations in the magnitude of Nelson's plurality. It has already increased as additional returns come in, until 4 o'clock this morning, with estimates from all but about half a dozen counties, and partial returns from those, it stands at 1,868. The first claims from the Kindred precincts were greatly exaggerated. With all his efforts in Grow Wing, Kindred only rolled up some 1,800 plurality, and no other county has given him one fourth so much. St. Louis is singularly close, Kindred having but a small majority. Nelson's largest plurality is some 5000 in Otter Tail. Stearns does not ent much of a figure, but he rolled 1000 votes in Stearns county. It will not be surprising if Nelson's plurality, after all the returns are in, shall reach 5000.

In spite of the complications in the legislative district, the PIONEER PRESS manages to print an approximately accurate and complete list of members of the next legislature. The Democratic gains are smaller than was expected in view of the many Republican splits. The few losses of this account have been offset by Republican gains in Democratic counties. The legislature will stand: Senate: Republicans, 45; Democrats, 10; Independents and Greenbackers, 3. House: Republicans, 70; Democrats, 70; Independents, 3. Wheat, Sargean, and Goodrich pulled through in Fillmore, Freeborn and Faribault; and Fletcher in Blue Earth, Bierman carried Judge Wilson through in his back in Winona, and Chandler is elected in Goodhue. The election of Truax in Dakota and Waite in Stearns are unexpected Republican gains. In the northern districts, Suckerman, Allison and Campbell are among the Kindred senators elected, and Consock and Stevenson among the friends of Nelson. It may be said that the friends of Windom form a considerable majority of the Republican members of the legislature.

No general consolidation of returns upon the bond act has been made, but in nearly every precinct shows majority for it; some almost unanimous, there is no shadow of doubt that it has been carried.

method of raising seed oysters is being
rapidly extended, and number of
steamers have recently been built at
